key_insight: LightHybridNet is a lightweight hybrid deep learning model that improved multi-label retinal disease classification from fundus images, especially in an imbalanced setting.
clinical_relevance: This approach may support earlier and more reliable automated screening of ophthalmic disease from routine fundus imaging, with explainability features to help interpretation.
method: Used the ODIR-5K fundus image dataset with 8 disease categories.
Applied preprocessing including histogram equalisation, colour space conversion, and contrast adjustment.
Used augmentation and a hybrid architecture with depthwise separable convolutions, compound scaling, and Grad-CAM interpretability.
evidence_signal: On the validation set, LightHybridNet achieved a weighted F1-score of 91.51%, macro AUC of 98.26%, and Cohen's Kappa of 90.14%, outperforming transfer-learning baselines.
watch_item: Performance was reported on a specific benchmark dataset, so external validation on other populations, devices, and clinical workflows is still needed before broad deployment.
paper_title: LightHybridNet: A Lightweight Hybrid Deep Learning Framework for Efficient Multi-Label Ophthalmic Disease Classification in Imbalanced Fundus Images
